title: ConceptSketchSpec
description: A drawing spec. Coordinate world: logical canvas 1000×750, Cartesian, y-up, origin bottom-left. Prefer a scene template (set template+params, see the scene catalog). Otherwise compose tier-2 elements. Commands interleave narration (speak) with drawing (draw) for a gradually built, narrated figure.

aspect.description: The screen shape, w:h: 4:3 (the default), 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, or any ratio from 1:3 to 3:1. The canvas keeps its short side 750 units.

heading.description: Top heading: omitted, the title (on a page with no card); a string, that text; false, none.

setting.description: Where it happens. ground: grass, sky, water, sand, soil, floor, desk, road, snow or night; "sky/grass" stacks two ("sky/soil/40": split 40 % down). props: pictures, place: left edge, right edge, top, bottom, top left…, along top, along bottom or beside <id>; repeat: a row.

page.description: valign: "center" (default) evens the space above and below the figure; "top"; "none". checks: keep or clear every check's own visuals after its answer (a quiz keeps).

role.description: thumbnail: the cast's listing picture, never played.

zoom_from.description: Playlist items only: the semantic-zoom entrance. Before this item begins, the PREVIOUS figure zooms into this element id (an id of the PREVIOUS item's scene) and fades there — so the new figure feels like the inside of the old one (heart → cell, bins → bell curve). Replaces the chapter card at that junction.

level.description: Difficulty of the explanation, when the request states one. Shown as a badge; omit if unspecified.

feedback.description: Questions' feedback: after the right/wrong line the player adds ONE short line for how well the viewer did. plain (default, nothing added), warm or dry; or {style, perfect, good, poor, none} with YOUR OWN lines per band (all right; two thirds; some; none) — a sentence or a list, in the cast's language, about its topic ("Good thing you're not a pharmacist."). {vars} work. An ask or quiz may set its own.

affirm.description: What a viewer hears after a RIGHT quiz answer. Omit (default): a short varied affirmation in the cast's language ("Spot on.", "Two in a row."). "playful": now and then a dry joke ("Suspiciously good."), for a light cast; "plain": the one word "Correct."; a list of your own short phrases; false: nothing.

record.description: false: keep no local record of the viewer's answers in their browser. Omit (default true).

voice.description: Narrator voice. Usually stamped from the #male/#female tags — omit unless the request states it. In dialogue this is speaker "a"; speaker "b" gets the contrasting voice.

stress.description: Stress marks drawn: all (default), new (only new words: glossed words, a turn's new words, elements with new: true), none. Speech keeps them.

shuffle.description: true: every quiz shuffles its choices (a quiz's own shuffle wins).

say_lang.description: BCP-47 tag of the language the `say` words are in, when it is not the narration's ("es" in a Spanish lesson narrated in English).

template.description: Scene template name from the catalog. Omit when composing elements directly.

params.description: Scene template parameters, per the catalog's parameter schema. A value may be a "{codeId.variable}" token naming a code element's script variable (or "{codeId.df.column}" for a DataFrame column) — the app substitutes the harvested value before drawing. Any template also takes "box": a region name — "left", "right", "top", "bottom" or "full" — that puts the whole figure in that part of the canvas so a code panel, an equation or a table can have the rest; or {x, y, w, h} in canvas units. Give it only when something else shares the page, and prefer the names.

domain.description: Domain coordinate ranges for quantitative diagrams, e.g. {"x": [0, 1000], "y": [0, 50]} for quantity/price. Curve exprs and point coordinates are in these units.

box.description: Where the chart sits: "auto" takes all the page your own drawing (shapes, paths, texts with x/y) leaves free — the choice beside a drawing of the thing it measures; or a region ("left", …) or {x, y, w, h}. Default: the whole page.

vars.description: Named numbers, e.g. {"f": 1}: curve expr reads them ("sin(f*x)"), bind computes fields from them, drawn text shows {f}, animate sweeps them. Never named x or like a function. {f} in a math tex is live: the paused viewer drags or types it. Object form {value, min, max, step, decimals, color, fixed: true}, or {expr: "a*b"} computed from earlier vars.

adjust.description: Move or enlarge a TEMPLATE's own parts, which are not your elements (its readout, its curve labels, a card): {"readout": {"move": [-20, 10], "scale": 1.4}} — move is [right, up] in percent of the page, scale grows the part about its center (0.5–2.5). Use a part id or group id from the template's element list.

details.description: The element `details` for ids that are not your own elements — a TEMPLATE's parts: {"demand_curve": "Here demand is $Q = 100 - 2P$ …"}.

authors.description: As cited: "Card and Krueger", "Jardim et al."

doi.description: Bare DOI (10.…), only one you are certain of.

url.description: Full https URL, only one you are certain of — NEVER invent or construct one; leave it out instead.

finding.description: What it found, in under ten words.

sources.description: The studies, reports and books the narration names ("a University of Washington team found…") — listed for the viewer in the tray, and linked from any element that `cites` one. Name every study you mention; a source without a link is still worth listing.

more.description: The viewer's corner list (default: the sources, bottom-right; false hides it). items: source ids and {title, url, text} extras.

items.description: One diagram element. The `type` decides which other properties apply. Tier 2 (preferred): axes, curve, point, arrow, label, region, node, edge — you describe relations, the renderer computes geometry. Tier 3 (escape hatch only): path, text, shape with explicit logical coordinates (1000×750, y-up, origin bottom-left). pinboard: a board of cards to keep a set in mind (players, clauses, evidence) — groups (≤ 3 labels), cards (≤ 8, by the board: a note {heading, lines, icon, token, date} or a document {title, text, source}, each with id, back, stamp, strike); each card is drawn by its id, <card>_stamp / <card>_strike by theirs, moved to <board>_slot_<group>_<k>, turned with turn.

id.description: Unique id, referenced by commands and other elements.

aspect.description: figure: its own shape (default 4:3) — its members' coordinates are in a canvas of that shape, the short side 750.

keep_frame.description: figure (written by Change the shape): fit its whole frame.

box.description: figure: where it goes — a region (left, right, top, bottom, full) or {x, y, w, h}; default the content area. Scaled evenly to fit, never stretched.

cross.description: axes: they cross at 0 when the domain contains it (default "origin"); "corner" keeps them at the plot's bottom-left.

steepness.description: curve: qualitative steepness — `medium` and `steep` draw nearly the same curve (the shape clips to the plot); `gentle` is the only visibly flatter one.

expr.description: curve: explicit function of x over the domain, e.g. "100 - 0.5*x". Use instead of direction/curvature when you know the function.

x_from.description: curve/region: start of the x interval (domain units; default: whole domain). region: {"ref": id} = that point's x, followed as it moves.

x_to.description: curve/region: end of the x interval. region: {"ref": "eq"} shades up to that point wherever it stands.

x_expr.description: curve: parametric x(t) — use with y_expr instead of expr, e.g. "cos(t)" for a circle.

y_expr.description: curve: parametric y(t), paired with x_expr.

t_from.description: curve: start of the parameter interval for x_expr/y_expr, domain units (default 0).

t_to.description: curve: end of the parameter interval for x_expr/y_expr, domain units (default 1).

data.description: [x, y] in data units — the page's domain, or a template's own axes.

canvas.description: point/angle: [x, y] in canvas units even on a page with a domain.

intersection_of.description: Two curve ids (your own or a scene template's); the point is their intersection.

on.description: point: the curve this point sits on at x (y is read off it).

anchor.description: A named point ON ref instead of its centre — e.g. {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_1"}: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

side.description: Place OUTSIDE ref's box on this side, gap units away.

gap.description: With side: distance from ref's box, logical units.

offset.description: [dx, dy] nudge applied after side/gap or anchor placement.

place.description: A named spot on the CANVAS, for a part that belongs to the page rather than to another element: the element's own same-named point lands on that point of the canvas's safe area, so "left" seats its left edge at the left margin, "center" centres it, and "top_right" tucks it into that corner — it can never fall off the edge, whatever its size. Its own `anchor` overrides which of ITS points lands there. Never with x/y or ref.

beside.description: An element id: placed next to it — to the right on a wide screen, below on a tall one (another side when there is no room). Like ref with side; never with x/y.

percent.description: [x, y] as percentages of the content area (y up): its centre (or its own `anchor`) lands there, whatever the screen's shape. Never with x/y or ref.

at.description: Where the element goes. point: x,y, or x + on (a curve id), or intersection_of.Others: ref + side/gap (outside another element's box) or ref + anchor (a named point on it); optional offset. Never with x/y. angle: the vertex — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else logical) or {ref, anchor} for a point on another element, e.g. {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_1"}.

guides.description: point: dashed lines to both axes. {values: true} also writes the point's x and y where they land; {x: "Q*", y: "P*"} writes that text instead.

anchor.description: With at: which of THIS element's anchors lands there (default opposite of at.side, else center).

canvas.description: [x, y] in canvas units, even on a domain page.

from.description: arrow/edge: endpoint (ref, x+y — domain units on a domain page — or canvas: [x, y] for page units); angle: the arm — a point ({ref, anchor} or [x, y]) or a direction in degrees counter-clockwise from +x — e.g. from: {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_2"}. pieces of triangles: the vertex to fan from ("vertex_1").

anchor.description: A named point ON ref instead of its centre — e.g. {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_1"}: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

data.description: [x, y] in data units — the page's domain, or a template's own axes.

canvas.description: [x, y] in canvas units, even on a domain page.

to.description: arrow/edge: endpoint (ref, x+y — domain units on a domain page — or canvas: [x, y] for page units); angle: the arm — a point ({ref, anchor} or [x, y]) or a direction in degrees counter-clockwise from +x — e.g. to: {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_3"}.

attach_to.description: label: id of the element this label belongs to. The renderer places it (collision-avoiding).

side.description: label: preferred side relative to the attached element. The collision solver may move it. measure: left/right of the segment's direction (default: away from the measured element).

href.description: link: the drawcast it opens — ./file.yaml, lecture:N, or a GitHub/Drive/player link the user gave; never invent one.

title.description: link: its words (default: the target's title). cards (compare): the words over the cards, or true/false (default: none under a heading).

image.description: link: a picture URL for the card.

form.description: link: card (default, a thumbnail) or text. math: {var}s as values (default), symbols or both.

open.description: link: auto (default: a new tab mid-video, this page at the end), tab, here, window (over the video).

link.description: Resource links for this element (a paper, a video, a book) — shown on its info card in the live player; the video export ignores them. Full https URLs, COPIED VERBATIM from the user's request — NEVER invent, guess, or construct a URL (a fabricated DOI or video id looks exactly like a real one). The kind is auto-detected: YouTube plays embedded, Wikipedia shows a summary, .pdf opens a document view, anything else a new tab. On a label, the link also reaches the element it attach_to's.

cites.description: Ids of top-level `sources` this element stands for — a claim, a number or a finding on the canvas; its info card then names and links the study behind it.

details.description: The formal detail behind this element, for a viewer who wants more: its equation, derivation, definition or caveat, in a few sentences — `$…$` for inline math, `$$…$$` on its own line for a display formula. Never narrated or drawn: in the live player hovering the element shows its first sentence with More ▸, and a click (which pauses) or right-click opens it all on the element's card. Only when the cast has something formal worth offering — at most a few per cast.

say.description: Words heard when the viewer taps this element (true: its own text); twice or held: 0.7×. Recorded with the narration — for a word or line worth hearing again.

speakers.description: dialogue: the two speakers — ids of elements you drew (icon, person, token), {"a": "tom", "b": "masha"}.

new.description: stress new: words that keep their marks.

turns.description: dialogue: a CONVERSATION as speech bubbles — the turns in order, {by: "a"|"b", text, gloss?} (gloss: a small grey translation under the words). Each is a bubble on its speaker's side, stacked down the page (at most six at once; older ones scroll away). A bare {"draw": "<id>"} draws the NEXT turn and, with no speak of its own, speaks it in its speaker's voice (a/b); give a speak to narrate over it instead. Parts: <id>_1 … (bubbles), <id>_1_words, <id>_1_gloss, <id>_on_a/b (the speaking mark); erase <id> takes all. Every bubble can be tapped to hear it again.

gloss.description: glossed: a TEXT TO READ in the language being learnt, each word with its translation — gloss is one per word of text, in order (punctuation stays with its word; "" for none). Every word can be tapped: it is spoken and a small popover gives its gloss. Parts: <id>_w_1 … (the words), <id>_g_1 … (glosses written), <id>_words; erase <id> takes all. colors work on it (word endings).

show_gloss.description: glossed: also WRITE the glosses small under the words — under: from the start (first exposure, the movie); after: once the read-first hold passes. dialogue: false — no glosses in the bubbles (the drill still cues with them).

gloss_size.description: glossed: the written glosses' size (default 0.6 × font_size).

read_first.description: glossed: after the text is drawn the cast holds on an "I've read it — play it ▸" pill (taps on words still work; 3 s in Watch and the movie) — then the next speak, usually the text read aloud.

practice.description: dialogue: true offers a drill after the last turn — the viewer plays one speaker, saying their turns (text, then gloss as cue, then memory over the reviews); every turn needs a gloss.

lang.description: dialogue: BCP-47 tag of the turns, for the speech recogniser (default: the cast's language).

stress.description: Stress marks drawn here, over the cast's stress.

new.description: stress new: true — its words are new and keep their marks; a list — just those words do (wherever they are shown).

work.description: scratch: a temporary WORKING card (grey paper) — one entry per line, words or {"tex": …} for a formula. Parts: <id>_box and <id>_line_1, _2 …; draw the box with the first line, then a line per beat as the narration builds the sum; afterwards erase it, fade it, or move it small into a corner (move with scale and to). It sits ON the figure; default: left middle, or at: {place: "top_right"} (any corner/side) or x/y. font_size sizes its lines (default 24; formulas scale with it, the card fits them). Several may share a page.

app_only.description: Drawn in the live player, left out of a video export (with every command's mention of it) — e.g. a small `text` "The math ▸" carrying `details`, placed for viewers to click.

between.description: region: two curve ids — your own curves OR a scene template's (e.g. demand_curve/supply_curve/ceiling_line in supply_demand, curve_<id> in qaly_profiles); the region is shaded between them (use x_from/x_to to limit; 0–100 axis units when no domain is declared).

target.description: annotation: the ids to mark (declare the annotation AFTER them). SEVERAL ids means ONE border around them all — the way to ring a cluster of marks, or box a word and its number together, without inventing a group for it.

kind.description: thumb: a thumbnail page's words or sticker. annotation: a PERMANENT mark — box or circle the conclusion, strike or cross out a rejected option. Default: box for text targets, circle otherwise. (Temporary attention = the highlight verb with glow, or point; area emphasis = region shading.)

shape.description: node/shape: decision=square, chance=circle, terminal=triangle (health-economics conventions); person = stick figure. x/y is the CENTRE of a node or shape, and width/height (circle: width = diameter) are honoured. population: "coin" — a counter of coins (a coin a billion) instead of people.

points.description: path: polyline points in logical coordinates (y-up) — in data units with `data: true`.

data.description: path/polygon: the points are in DATA units (the page's domain, or a template's own axes) — an overlay that lands on the chart it annotates.

smooth.description: path: smooth curve through the points (Catmull-Rom).

members.description: group: element ids that form one thing; draw/move/highlight the group id to act on all.

layout.description: group: ARRANGE the members — "row" side by side, "column" stacked, "auto" a row on a wide screen and a column on a tall one, "grid" `columns` wide, or, with no `columns`, as wide as shows the members largest. Every position is computed from the members' own sizes, so a structure of boxes needs NO x/y anywhere: declare the parts, wrap them in a group with a layout, and join them with arrows. Boxes in a laid-out group are given one size (the largest needed) so the row reads as a row. `gap` (default 40) spaces them, `align` (center/start/end) sets the cross axis. Combine with `fit` to scale the finished arrangement into a region. population: "grid" (default) or "crowd" (people standing about).

gap.description: group layout: space between neighbours, logical units (default 40).

columns.description: group layout grid: members per row. Leave it out and the grid picks the count that shows the members largest. table: the header row, one string per column.

row_headers.description: table: the first column is row headers, smaller and softer (default: when columns starts with "").

walk.description: group: the members are gone through one at a time. true/"fade": peers (kinds of bridge) — drawing the next fades the ones shown; a command across two or more, or the group, brings them back. "zoom": the same, and the camera frames each as it arrives, pulling back for a comparison. "replace": alternatives in ONE place (a straight frontier, then the bowed one) — the next erases the one before; a command naming several draws them back. Replaces writing those commands.

equalize.description: group layout: one size for every member that draws a border (default true).

fit.description: group: scale and centre the members into this region or box (aspect kept). population: the region or box it fills (legend included).

tex.description: math: LaTeX, drawn as handwriting; {v} writes var v's value, live (an argument needs {{v}}: \frac{{B}}{…}, ^{{t}}). label: LaTeX instead of text.

size.description: cards: "auto" (default) or a factor 0.6–2. math: font size, the same units as text font_size (default 28, a label's size). Leave it out: every formula on a page shares one size; at most a headline formula may take 34. icon: box size in logical units (default 100). music: one staff space in logical units (default 26). link: card width (300). dialogue: a factor on its words (1; up to 2).

symbol.description: music: the symbol, drawn from a real music font — notes join their stems exactly. x/y is its centre (a note's head).

stem.description: music: a note's stem direction (default up).

dots.description: music: dots after a note (each adds half).

time.description: music: the time signature for symbol time, e.g. "3/4".

steps.description: math: a DERIVATION — the lines after `tex`, each written by one {"step": id} beat (copied down, morphed glyph by glyph); {"tex", "note"} adds a note beside the line. Lines are <id>_2, <id>_3, …; notes <id>_2_note. cards (rank): true — numbered slots joined by arrows.

step_gap.description: math with steps: canvas units between lines (default ≈ 3.2 × size).

note_dx.description: math with steps: the notes' column, canvas units right of the formula's centre (default 220).

colors.description: math: colour per term, a TeX snippet → colour ({"x": "#2f6b8f", "\\Delta C": "#b5482e"}); every occurrence. population: colour per state (hex or a palette name). text, label, node: colour part of the words, a literal piece → colour ({"А$": "#2f6b8f"}), every occurrence; ^ at the start anchors to the start of a word, $ at the end to its end ("А$" is the last А of МАМА, "^при" a prefix); the stress mark is ignored when matching.

set.description: icon: icon set prefix (lucide, tabler, ph, heroicons, material-symbols; fa6-solid, twemoji as CC BY).

credit.description: image/icon/node (its icon): attribution (machine-written; copy VERBATIM if present).

crop.description: inset: true (default) fits the source page's ink into the box so the drawing fills it; false fits the whole 1000×750 canvas, so every uncropped inset shares one scale and the source's layout is preserved.

x.description: text/shape/sector/arc/polygon/pieces/ellipse: logical x (y-up canvas) — the centre, for the shapes that have one. inset: the centre of the box; omit x, y and at to take the next slot in the right-hand thumbnail column.

y.description: text/shape/sector/arc/polygon/pieces/ellipse: logical y (y-up canvas) — the centre, for the shapes that have one. inset: the centre of the box; omit x, y and at to take the next slot in the right-hand thumbnail column.

width.description: text: wrap the words into rows this wide. shape rect / node / portrait / source / code / pieces strips+grid (the rectangle to cut): width in logical units (a source defaults to 200 for a cover, 260 for a page; a code panel to 880). / image: width. inset: box width (default 160; the height follows 4:3 unless given) — only read when x/y or at place the inset; in the column, width and height are ignored.

height.description: shape rect / node / pieces strips+grid (the rectangle to cut): height in logical units. inset: box height. image: its height, the width following the picture's shape (a tall painting: height ~620, x off-centre, so its details fit beside it); width wins when both are given.

radius.description: shape circle / sector / arc / regular polygon / pieces / angle: radius in logical units (angle default 40). point: the dot's radius in canvas units (default 7; e.g. 20 for a ball) — bind it to animate. node rect: corner radius (default 0).

shadow.description: node rect: true = a soft shadow behind the box (for a filled box).

or.description: icon: keywords tried in order when of finds none ("guinea pig" → ["hamster"]).

icon.description: node rect: an icon inside the box, above its text — a keyword ("shark"), a list tried in order, or {"of", "set", "or"}; the box grows to fit.

icon_strokes.description: node rect: the resolved icon (machine-written; copy VERBATIM if present).

icon_key.description: node/icon: what the icon was resolved for (machine-written; copy VERBATIM if present).

icon_side.description: node rect/cards: the icon over the text (top) or beside it (left; a match's default).

flip.description: icon: mirrored left-right, so the picture faces the other way (a car driving left).

icon_look.description: node/cards/icon: picture (its own artwork; nodes/cards default) or drawn (traced; icon default) — drawn only when the icon is the subject; line (icon element only: thin ink strokes, tabler/lucide — beside a board label; a spine slot's icon is always line).

with.description: icon: drawn right after this element (an icon beside a label)

font_size.description: text: font size, logical units (≥ 14; default 26). node: text size (24; a text-fitted box grows). scale: numbers (22).

start.description: sector/arc: start angle in degrees, counter-clockwise from +x (0 = right, 90 = up) — e.g. start: 0, end: 90 is the upper-right quarter.

end.description: sector/arc: end angle in degrees, counter-clockwise from +x — e.g. start: 0, end: 90 is the upper-right quarter.

sides.description: polygon: sides of a REGULAR polygon centred at x,y with radius — instead of points.

counts.description: pieces blocks / dots: the columns, left to right, each this many unit cells — [1, 2, 3, 4] is a staircase. Pieces <id>_1 … column by column, from the foot of each.

cell.description: pieces blocks / dots: one cell's side in logical units (default 50).

hang.description: pieces blocks / dots: the columns hang from the top of a box `rows` cells high (default the tallest column) — a second staircase [4, 3, 2, 1] hung at the same x, y with rows 5 fills the 4 × 5 rectangle the first one leaves.

rotation.description: polygon/ellipse: turn by this many degrees (polygon: the regular polygon; ellipse: its major axis, counter-clockwise from +x).

n.description: pieces: how many pieces to cut — e.g. 12 sectors of a circle, 4 strips of a rectangle, or the COLUMNS of a grid (rows in `rows`; n: 1 with rows: 4 gives four horizontal bands). Each becomes its own element <id>_1 … <id>_n that move, arrange and highlight can name; `draw: ["<id>"]` draws them all.

icon.description: a line icon above the slot, only when clear (crown = autocracy, wheat = bread)
a line icon above the slot, only when clear (crown = autocracy, wheat = bread)
a line icon above the slot, only when clear (crown = autocracy, wheat = bread)

rows.description: pieces grid: how many rows (n is the columns) — e.g. n: 4, rows: 3 cuts a rectangle into twelve cells, numbered row by row from the top left. At most 256 cells in all. spine: its rows {long, short, trigger} (two or three), each {label (a word or two), sub, slots: [words, or {text, note}]} — 1 to 5 slots, a trigger at most 3. table: a GRID OF WORDS (an endings table, a conjugation) — rows is a list of rows, each a list of cell strings ([["Кто? Что?", "сто́л", "столы́"], ["Где?", "в столе́", "в стола́х"]]); columns is the header row (["", "singular", "plural"]; "" first = the first column is row headers). Cells are <id>_r1c2 (rows and columns from 1, the header not counted), rows <id>_r1, columns <id>_c2, the header and rules <id>_head. {"draw": "<id>"} draws it all — unless commands draw its rows or cells: then it draws the frame and header alone, and the rows come as drawn. colors colour endings in the cells; say: true makes every cell tappable to hear. x, y: its centre (default the page's); it shrinks to fit the width.

label.description: angle/measure: the text — angle default the degrees ("62°"); false hides it; measure default "{value}" e.g. "b = {value}"; a measure label without {value} is drawn as written.

right.description: angle: draw the right-angle square (default: automatically when the angle is 90°).

what.description: measure: what to read — length (a segment, arrow or path), width / height (of the element's box), area or perimeter (of its outline). Default: length for a segment, area for a closed shape.

unit.description: measure / scale: appended to the value — "cm", "%", "USD".

scale.description: measure: logical units per unit (default 1) — 50 with unit cm makes a 100-unit side read 2.0 cm.

decimals.description: measure: decimals shown (default 0 when the value is 100 or more, else 1).

offset.description: measure: how far the dimension line sits from the segment (default 24).

rx.description: ellipse: half-axis along +x before rotation, logical units (default 150).

ry.description: ellipse: half-axis along +y before rotation, logical units (default 100).

items.description: line: a point it passes through — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

through.description: line: one or two points the line passes through — [{"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_1"}, {"ref": "tri", "anchor": "vertex_2"}] extends a side; with one point give slope or angle.

slope.description: line: rise over run in domain units when a domain is declared, else logical.

angle.description: line: direction in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (not the angle element type — this is the `line` element's own direction field). thumb: its turn, the same way.

of.description: portrait: the person's name, e.g. "John Maynard Keynes" — the app resolves it to their Wikipedia portrait and traces it into sketch strokes, and draws this name as a centered caption with the photo automatically (do NOT add a separate label element for the name). Use a portrait SPARINGLY, only when the person or history genuinely serves the topic; place it small (width ~150-200) off to a side with x/y. NEVER invent an image url; only copy a url the user's request explicitly provided. source: the WORK'S TITLE, e.g. "The Wealth of Nations" — the PREFERRED reference, because the app verifies it against Wikipedia, so a wrong title fails visibly (a wrong doi/isbn resolves to the wrong work in silence). It is also drawn as the caption under the picture, so never add a label element for it. pieces: what to cut — "sectors" (a circle of radius at x, y), "strips" (a width × height rectangle centred on x, y, n vertical strips), "grid" (the same rectangle, n columns × rows rows), "rings" (n concentric rings of a circle of radius at x, y — unroll them with arrange), "triangles" (fans a regular polygon (sides + radius) or a polygon (points, from: "vertex_k") into triangles), "halving" (halves a width × height rectangle n times, alternately, with `<id>_rest` the remainder — 1/2 + 1/4 + …), or "blocks" / "dots" (unit squares / dots in columns of `counts` — a staircase, an array, a triangular number — centred on x, y or placed for you; no n). measure: the element to measure. image: what to photograph (a Commons/Wikipedia title). icon: a keyword. inset: the playlist item whose final frame this shows — its title (case-insensitive), its 1-based number as a string ("2"), or "previous".

url.description: portrait/source/image: direct image, .pdf, or YOUTUBE url — ONLY when the user's request supplied one (copy it verbatim; never invent). On a source, a YouTube url draws the video's still, framed with a hand-drawn play mark, and clicking it plays the video embedded — use it when the video IS a thing the figure points at, and note that its title becomes the caption automatically.

look.description: image: "screen" keeps colour and resolution — screenshots, diagrams, paintings you point into. cards: paper (default), flat or outline (plain boxes). pinboard: row (default) or columns.

view.description: image: the part shown, [x, y, w, h] fractions from the top-left. figure (written by Change the shape): the part of its coordinates fitted into its box.

regions.description: image: named parts, name → [x, y, w, h] fractions of the whole picture from the top-left. Target one as "<id>:<name>"; any spot as "<id>@[x, y, w, h]" or "<id>@[x, y]". "auto" (or {auto: {detail, kinds, find}}) asks the app to find the parts; aim only at names the app listed — never guess one.

strokes.description: portrait/source: embedded traced strokes (machine-written; copy VERBATIM if present, never edit or regenerate).

doi.description: source: DOI of a paper, e.g. "10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762" — resolved to its open-access PDF. COPY IT from the user's request; NEVER invent or reconstruct a DOI: a wrong-but-real DOI silently shows the wrong paper.

isbn.description: source: ISBN of a book — resolved to its Open Library cover. Copy it from the user's request; never invent one.

archive.description: source: Internet Archive scan id (the id in an archive.org/details/… URL) — a public-domain scan, any page. Copy it from the user's request; never invent one.

page.description: source: which page to show — the 1-based page of a PDF, or (with archive) the scan's LEAF index, which usually differs from the printed page number by however much front matter the book has. Only meaningful on a doi/pdf/archive source.

quote.description: source: the passage ON that page to sweep with a highlighter, in drawcast's own ink, timed to the narration (draw "<id>_quote" as its own beat). Must be VERBATIM text the user supplied or that certainly appears on that page — a paraphrase simply will not highlight. Needs page, and a PDF source (doi or a .pdf url).

cameo.description: portrait: cameo presentation — centered, larger and frameless with a fast fade, made to APPEAR on the beat that first names the person and be ERASED a beat or two later. Omit x/y/width in cameo mode unless you need them. Off = the small framed corner fixture.

caption.description: portrait: the name drawn under the photo — false (or "") for none (a cameo the narration names), or other words to write; default: the of name.

reveal.description: portrait/source: how a photo or page enters — and, played backwards by erase, exits. wipe = top-down like a print emerging (the default; omit unless you want another), develop = darkroom blur-to-sharp, iris = circle opening from the center, drift = slightly large settling into place, fade = plain opacity.

file.description: image: a PINNED Wikimedia Commons file — its title with the File: prefix ("File:Petrograd 1917.jpg"), shown exactly, never searched. Only a file someone has SEEN; copy it verbatim if present. Otherwise search Commons and pin one yourself, after looking.

pexels.description: image: a pinned Pexels photo id — timeless scenery only (snow, fire, paper), never a picture of the event; meta then carries no date or place.

file_thumb.description: image/screen with file: the pinned thumb — copy VERBATIM with its file; never write one.

file_film.description: film (file + clip): its pinned record — copy VERBATIM with its file; never write one.

opens.description: image: full — the line that draws it shows the picture over the whole page, drifting slowly toward its first region, with its date · place from meta written small; before the next line it settles into its place and its frame draws in. One or two per cast, for pictures that set a scene; never mark it on its opening line.

meta.description: image: what the picture IS, from its file's own record (copy VERBATIM if present; never guess): date and place make its caption, licence and credit its line in the Sources corner.

clip.description: image, a film (a pinned .webm/.ogv file): [from, to] in seconds — the shot it plays, muted, for the line that draws it (looping if the line is longer). Copy VERBATIM if present.

hold.description: image, a film: the second inside clip it stops on and stays as a still — read, mark or frame it from the NEXT line. A whole second (a fraction rounds). Default: the last whole second before the clip's end.

language.description: code: the runtime that executes the script. brython = the light tier (loads in about a second): CPython syntax and standard library, plus pandas, plotly.express, numpy, matplotlib, scipy.stats, statsmodels and seaborn emulations — the default for a script that needs no heavy numerics. python = full CPython via pyodide (real numpy/scipy/matplotlib, PyPI on demand; tens of megabytes). r = R via webR (base or tidyverse; library() auto-installs; every top-level expression prints as at the console; a trailing data frame draws as a table, a base plot or a printed ggplot as a figure). basic = Commodore 64 BASIC V2, drawcast's own small interpreter: PRINT, variables, GOTO/GOSUB, IF/THEN, FOR/NEXT, POKE/PEEK to the screen, colour RAM, border (53280) and background (53281); the run leaves a 40 × 25 C64 screen that is DRAWN on the panel — pair it with frame: "c64". No arrays, DATA, INPUT, SYS or sound in this first cut.

code.description: code: the script, one newline-separated string. It EXECUTES for real in the viewer's browser at figure-preparation time, so keep it short (≤ ~14 lines), deterministic (SEED any randomness), print() exactly the numbers the narration mentions, and end with at most ONE plot — matplotlib, or plotly express left in a variable (fig = px.bar(...)); packages auto-install (numpy/pandas/matplotlib ship with the runtime; pure-Python PyPI packages like plotly install on demand). Each line becomes a drawable `<id>_line_1` … `<id>_line_N` and the whole output panel is `<id>_out` — reveal lines with draw on their own narration beats, then draw the output. A script can also FEED a template: any params value written as "{<this id>.<variable>}" is replaced by that variable after the run (lists, numbers, dicts, a DataFrame as {columns, rows}); with show: "none" the element draws nothing and only supplies data.

show.description: code: where the CODE sits relative to its output — output (just the result; the default for a script without controls), left / right (code pane on that side, 55 % of the width; give the element width ≥ 700), above / below (code pane stacked over or under the output at full width — pair with lines on a long script; below is the default for a script WITH controls: output on top, code under it), code (the script alone), none (draws NOTHING — the script only feeds template params through "{id.var}" tokens).

lines.description: code: show the script through a window this many lines tall (≥ 3); stepping past the window scrolls it, as an editor does. Use with above/below, or whenever a script runs long.

frame.description: code: chrome drawn around the panel — none (bare paper, no frame at all; THE DEFAULT), screen (the code and its output on a computer display: one rounded shell with a chin, no stand), crt (an old tube monitor: chunky shell, bulging glass, little buttons on the chin, on a short foot), c64 (that tube monitor standing on a home-computer keyboard, the 1982 desk), laptop (the flat display over a keyboard), window (a title bar with three dots), panel (just a light frame). Ask for the screen when the story is that this happened on a computer, and pair it with draw: {mode: "type"} so the code is typed onto it. image: tv (a television set), print (a photograph, corner tape), poster (pinned at the top), newspaper (a masthead rule over it), none (the default) — drawn round the picture after it.

figures.description: code: how many separate figures the script produces (2 or more; omit for none or one). Each plt.figure() stage becomes its own drawable `<id>_fig_1` … `<id>_fig_K`, ALL SHARING ONE FRAME — drawing the next replaces the previous, so a parameter change or a chart built stage by stage plays as narrated beats. Keep xlim/ylim FIXED across stages so the swap reads as the chart itself changing.

chart.description: code: how a matplotlib chart LOOKS — THE DEFAULT IS xkcd: matplotlib's hand-drawn wobble, lettered in the app's own handwriting, so the chart is drawn in the same hand as the rest of the figure. Force another: seaborn (a calm grid, the figure's own ink and series colours on the drawing's paper) or plain (matplotlib's own defaults). Only `language: "python"` has a real matplotlib to style; the light tiers draw their charts through an emulation and ignore it.

feel.description: code: how the script's CHART looks. drawcast: in the drawing's own ink, palette and paper (matplotlib hand-drawn, ggplot themed). native: the library's own defaults, as in an IDE — for a lesson ABOUT the code. Default: native when the code is on screen, drawcast otherwise. Printed output is always typewriter.

game.description: code: a Commodore 64 program on the machine — pair it with frame: "c64" (or "crt"). Write a KEY from drawcast's own catalogue — c64maze (A 3D maze to find your way out of, written in C — the most-starred open C64 game on GitHub.); crowboy (A side-scrolling beat-em-up demo: sprites, scrolling, a joystick.); space-shooter (A vertical shooter from the RetroGameDev book's example, extended.); tenlander (A lunar lander in ten lines of BASIC — 749 bytes, and it LISTs.); wolfling (A small platform game — the demo vc64web's own documentation ships.); invaders (Space-invaders in XC-BASIC, the compiled BASIC dialect's own example — fire to start.); puralax (A colour-flooding puzzle game, ported to the C64 in XC-BASIC by Csaba Fekete — F1 to start.); c-rex (Chrome's no-internet dinosaur runner, rebuilt for the C64 with music by LFT — fire to jump.); ronino (A board-game duel against the computer (NegaMax with alpha-beta pruning), written in C with Oscar64.); 3d-cube (A wireframe cube you rotate in real time — F2 to start, F1 for the keys. A demo, not a game.); panopticon (A demoscene demo from Revision 2014: effects and music, no controls — sit back and watch.); diffusion (Particles diffusing across a grid, live — a tiny KickC simulation, no controls.); nono-pixie (A nonogram puzzle cartridge with 100 puzzles, by Carl-Henrik Skårstedt (2019) — fire to start.); space-orbs (A co-operative falling-orbs puzzle for two, by Space Moguls Games (2019).) — or an https URL to a .prg/.d64/.t64 ONLY when the user's request supplied one; never invent a URL. The screen shows the machine's blue boot screen with a play mark on it; while the app is paused a click on the mark starts the program in a real C64 emulator over the figure, sound and joystick included, and the ⊕ tray lets the viewer pick another program from the same catalogue. App only: a movie shows the drawn screen.

marks.description: code: pen passes over the script, each its OWN beat `<id>_mark_1`, `<id>_mark_2`, … drawn in the order written — so a line of narration can say "and this is where the seed goes in" while the marker travels across exactly that phrase. Each item is a VERBATIM piece of a drawn line: a whole line, or just the part you are talking about (`"rng.default_rng(7)"`). A plain string is the yellow highlighter; `{"text": "...", "kind": "strike"}` crosses it out and `"underline"` underlines it. The text must sit on ONE line as one piece (a wrapped line is two rows on screen); the first occurrence wins, so write more of the line when a short phrase repeats. Draw them like any other id: {"draw": ["sim_mark_1"], "speak": "…"} — and erase to take the pen off again.

code_result.description: code: machine-written execution result (copy VERBATIM if present; never write, edit, or invent it).

code_src.description: code: machine-written (copy VERBATIM if present; never write it).

controls.description: code: names of variables the viewer may change from the ⊕ tray. Each is born ONCE in the script as a control literal — a range tuple (min, max) or (min, max, step) becomes a slider (integers when written without decimal points), a list of strings a choice row, True/False a switch, a string a text field, a bare number a number field (never a guessed range) — or as Slider(1, 50, default=10, label="Cycles") / Choice("a", "b") / Toggle(False) / Text("x") / Number(3) / Button("Roll again") when a label or default is wanted. The default (midpoint of a range) is what the movie shows. Prefer controls to an explore beat that tells the viewer to edit the script.

autorun.description: code: re-run the script on every control change (default true); false shows a Run button in the tray instead.

pane.description: code: what the pane holds — code (THE DEFAULT: the script's lines) or controls (the script's `controls` drawn as knobs and switches — a slider as a track with a knob, a choice as chips, a toggle as a switch — live while paused; the movie shows them at their defaults). The pane sits UNDER the output by default (show: below, full width); set show only when the request wants it elsewhere.

count.description: population: how many people (default: the states' sum, else 100).

min.description: scale: the left end of the number line.

max.description: scale: the right end of the number line.

value.description: scale: the TRUE value — a marker over the line with its number, the part <id>_answer. A scale is a number line to GUESS ON: draw <id> (the line, ticks and numbers), then ask with on: <id> — the viewer clicks where they think the value lies, and the marker slides from their guess to the truth. For a year (min 1700, max 1800), a share (unit "%", 0–100), or an amount spanning orders of magnitude (log: true). Placed by the page, or by at: {percent: [x, y]} (the line's centre) or {place}, or x, y (the left end); width sets its length; label is a caption over the line.

log.description: scale: logarithmic spacing (min > 0) — one tick per power of ten.

items.description: sequence: the pictures in turn — {icon, label} (icon a keyword or fallbacks ["brick", "wall"]), {text, label} for a paper card, or the id of an element you drew; mark: a short verdict word or a colour, shown under it in the strip once done; cites: source ids, as on any element. cards: cards the viewer ORDERS or SORTS, asked with an ask on: <id> (rank: they drag the cards and press Answer, and the cards slide into the true order; sort: every card, then Done shows the answer — check: "each" judges each drop, a wrong card moved to its box). RANK: the items in their TRUE order, first = most/earliest/top (a word or three each: "USA", "Norway"), with ends naming the two ends. SORT: give bins, and each item {text, bin} (the viewer drags or TAPS a card to send it to a box); deck: true deals up to 30 cards one at a time. TAP ALL THE …: give select (the one box's title) and items {text, in: true} for those that belong; the rest stay out. 2–8 items, up to 30 with deck. The cards are drawn SHUFFLED, so draw <id> before the ask; after it they stand in the true order. Cards are <id>_1 … in true order; sort's boxes <id>_bin_1 …. An item {text, icon: "shark"} draws an icon on its card (match_icon: on its partner).

bins.description: cards: the boxes to sort into (a word or two each); every item's bin is one of them.

ends.description: cards (rank): what the two ends mean, first end first: ["most", "least"], ["earliest", "latest"].

arrange.description: cards: rank — a row (default) or a column (longer names); sort, select, deck — drop (default: the cards above the boxes; y is the top of the cards), side (the cards a column on the left, the boxes right; up to 8 cards) or rise (the boxes above the cards; y is the boxes' top).

along.description: cards: PLACE ON A SCALE — the id of a scale element; each item has a value, and the viewer drags the cards onto the line ("put these inventions on the timeline"). Draw the scale and the cards first.

compare.description: cards: HIGHER OR LOWER — the question each pair answers, written over the cards ("Which kills more people a year?"); each item has a value; pairs of items (pairs, default consecutive) are rows, the viewer taps the bigger of each, and its numbers appear.

pairs.description: cards (compare): which items face each other, as 0-based index pairs [[0, 1], [2, 3]] (default consecutive).

options.description: cards: DECIDE — the choices (a few words each), each with goto: the label of the section that plays out its consequences. The viewer taps one and the cast goes there; best: true on one makes the decision scored. Movies play every branch in order, so write each to stand on its own ("If you treat now: …"). Give then: the label where the branches meet.

select.description: cards: TAP ALL THE … — the title of the one box ("Mammals"); items {text, in: true} belong in it, the rest ({text, in: false} or a plain string) stay out. The viewer taps the cards that belong (each judged as tapped), then Done. Not with bins.

rule.description: cards: ODD ONE OUT — 3–6 items, one {text, odd: true}: the viewer taps the one that does not belong (ask on: <id>); rule says what the others share, written under the cards as the odd one is ringed ("All four are mammals; the shark is a fish.").

deck.description: cards (sort): a DECK — one large card at a time in the middle; the viewer taps a box (or presses 1, 2, …), the card flies there and the next comes, with a ✓ or ✗ for each. Up to 30 items: for many quick calls.

check.description: cards (sort, select, deck): end (default) — sort every card, then Done shows the answer; each — every card judged as it is dropped, a wrong one moved to its right box.

then.description: cards (decide): the label where every branch meets again — a live viewer who chose one branch skips the others and goes on here. spine: the outcome its rows lead to ("War, 1939").

strip.description: sequence: where done items wait, small — top (default), bottom, none.

show_upcoming.description: sequence: dots — a placeholder in each slot not reached yet.

recap.description: sequence: false keeps the row at the top when <id>_strip is drawn (default: it comes to the middle, larger).

ticks.description: scale: tick intervals (default 5). axes: true (round numbers from the domain) or per axis {"x": [1600, 1800], "y": true}.

tick_format.description: scale: words (default: "43 million"), numerals, or power (10ⁿ).

era.description: scale: negative years as BC (default), BCE, or none (minus).

markers.description: scale: extra labelled points on the line ({value: 7, label: "old limit"}) — the engine places the words; drawn with the line (or draw <id>_marker_<n>).

slider.description: scale: set by an ask's estimate — never write it.

states.description: population: a GROUP OF PEOPLE drawn as person icons — for epidemics, vaccination, screening, risk, trials; never dots. People per state, in order: {"healthy": 70, "sick": 20, "immune": 10} — the FIRST is the remainder. Built-in looks: healthy, sick, immune, vaccinated, dead; any other state needs a colour in colors. Each state is a set <id>_<state> (all the people in it now — highlight or focus it), plus <id>_legend; text reads {<id>.sick}, {<id>.count}. Everyone keeps their place: animate a count (bind: {"states.sick": "i"} with a var i) and people turn over one by one. A later state never takes an earlier one's people — list vaccinated before sick and the infection reaches only the unvaccinated. Place it with fit (a region) or x, y, width, height.

order.description: population: which people a state takes — spread (evenly mixed; default), cluster (outward from one seed person: an outbreak), random, rows (filled from the top left: "8 in 100"). One for all, or per state: {"vaccinated": "spread", "sick": "cluster"}.

seed.description: population: picks the cluster's first person and the random order (same seed, same people).

legend.description: population: a legend under the people, "70 healthy" per state (default true).

labels.description: population: the legend's word per state (default the state's name).

params.description: timeline: a timeline on the board, beside anything (a world_map too) — events (each with an id: its part is <id>_event_<event id>), eras, view {from, to}, and magnify {from, to}: that span drawn again below on a wider axis, with a lens between (<id>_lens, <id>_zoom); <id>_axis is the axis. Placed with fit (default full).

group.description: A group's label, or its number from 1.

icon_strokes.description: Machine-written, as icon_key and credit; never write them.

token.description: A portrait or icon token's id: its picture shown round on the card.

ground.description: pinboard: what the cards lie on.

bind.description: Numeric fields computed from vars: {"end": "30 + 60*f", "at.x": "t"} — a field or a dot path to a number; the written value is the start.

fill_style.description: polygon/sector/ellipse/closed path fill: hatch (default, hand-drawn strokes) or wash (one flat translucent tint, like a circle's — a sunlit half); opacity sets its strength (default 0.35).

draw.description: How this element animates when drawn.

mode.description: sketch = progressive handwriting-style drawing; instant = appears at once; type = characters appear at typing speed with a cursor (code lines only — on any other element it draws as sketch); fade = fades in.

elements.description: Tier-2/3 elements (also allowed alongside a template, for annotations).

items.description: One playback command: ONE action verb (draw / pause / wait / quiz / ask / label / if / explore / show / hide / erase / clear / highlight / point / move / arrange / fade / flip / morph / copy / flow / keep / camera / animate / run), optionally WITH speak to narrate it — voice and action start together and the command ends when BOTH finish. Or speak alone (a rare standalone line, e.g. the closing synthesis). Commands run strictly in sequence; each completes before the next begins (except a standalone speak with blocking:false).

speak.description: Narration sentence, spoken aloud and shown as a caption. Alongside an action verb it narrates that action simultaneously (the preferred style: {"draw": ["supply"], "speak": "This is the supply curve."}). Alone, it is a standalone narration line. A word in ANOTHER language is marked [de:ich] or [french:c'est la vie] — code or English name, or a full locale ([cs-CZ:ahoj]) for a language outside that list — and is then spoken by a voice of that language; the caption shows just the word.

cue.description: With speak: WHEN in the sentence the action starts — 0 the first word, 0.5 half way, 1 the last. For an action that belongs to a MOMENT in the line; without it the action runs with the whole sentence (the normal case). Commands right after it with their own cue and no speak are cued in the same line: several draws, each on its word.

cue_end.description: With cue: the cue is where the action has FINISHED, not where it starts — the reveal lands its last stroke on that word. Use it for a completion ("…and the curve is back where it began"); not for a gesture or a stream, where the START is the event.

blocking.description: With speak: false starts the narration and continues at once: gestures and animate run under it; a draw or erase waits for it.

caption.description: With speak: false — heard, not read: no caption (a listen ask's clip says "🎧 Listen…") until the next question is answered or a show_caption.

show_caption.description: Bring up the words of the last line spoken with caption: false.

voice.description: With speak in a dialogue: which speaker reads this line — "a" (the lead/teacher, the default) or "b" (the second voice). Also on a quiz/ask, speak or not: that speaker reads its question and right/wrong.

delivery.description: With speak (or a quiz/ask): named delivery nudge — grave = slow and weighty for the key reveal; brisk = lightly quicker for recaps. Mark only the few lines where the meaning warrants it.

fill.description: GAPS: write the [gaps] of these texts in, without asking.

draw.description: Element ids to draw. Listed elements animate one after another unless parallel is true. A template may also name a SET of its own ids (a chess board's "position", "pieces", "squares" — its catalog entry lists them): naming one draws every member, and each member still answers to its own id for everything else.

parallel.description: With draw/erase: animate the listed elements simultaneously.

turn.description: pinboard: turn that card over to its back (a narrated flip); again to turn it back.

wait.description: Wait until the viewer clicks before continuing — a reveal gate ('study this… now click') or an act boundary. Auto-resolved in video export. read: a reading hold (a glossed text's read_first makes it).

quiz.description: Pose a multiple-choice question. The question is spoken and captioned; in the app the viewer answers on buttons (required: true means it cannot be skipped); in video export it auto-reveals after a beat and never waits. correct is 1-BASED.

question.description: The question, spoken aloud and shown as the caption.

intro.description: Optional spoken introduction ('Time for a quick check!'), prepended to the question line. Introduce a quiz HERE, never in a separate speak command — viewers can skip questions, and a skipped question must take its introduction with it.

choices.description: 2-4 short answer options, a few words each.

right.description: One sentence stating the answer and the reason. Spoken on a correct answer, AND as the reveal after a wrong answer or in a movie — so no praise words ('The price rises — more buyers compete'), never ('Exactly!').

wrong.description: Spoken on a wrong answer, before the correct one is revealed. One sentence.

required.description: App only: the question cannot be skipped without answering. Movies never wait.

shuffle.description: Choices in a fixed mixed order; correct is for the order as written.

say_answer.description: After the answer, the right option is spoken in its own language — on by default for an option in another script than the narration; true for a Latin-script lesson (Spanish), false never.

right_goto.description: Jump to this label on a correct VIEWER answer. Movies always play straight through.

wrong_goto.description: Jump to this label on a wrong VIEWER answer — typically back to the explanation, so the viewer re-watches and the question comes again. Movies always play straight through.

store.description: Store the chosen option's TEXT under this simple name (letters, digits, underscores; starts with a letter): later speak lines may use {name}, {name.ok} (true/false) and {name.secs} (seconds the viewer took). Movies and skipped questions store the correct option.

feedback.description: This question's own feedback (as the top-level feedback; wins over it).

on_canvas.description: true: the choices are buttons drawn on the figure; the question is not said again (say it in the line before).

buttons.description: on_canvas: each choice's text and icon.

say_question.description: on_canvas: true speaks and shows the question.

keep_buttons.description: on_canvas: true keeps the buttons after the answer.

reveal.description: A stamp ("MYTH", "46 hours!") drawn beside the figure WITH the right line — no draw after the quiz. true = the right choice's words. {text, at, color, size, style: stamp|label, keep}. It goes when its figure is hidden.

reveal_at.description: Where the reveal stamp goes: an element id (on it) or {x, y}.

above.description: Element id(s) shown with the question, in a band above the card (drawn for it; they leave with it). Not with on_canvas.

below.description: Element id(s) that land with the answer, in a band under the card (with the reveal stamp). Not with on_canvas.

frame.description: true: the card stays put and its reveal stamp lands under it (implied by above/below). Not with on_canvas.

confidence.description: true: a bet on how sure after the pick; {calib}, {calib.score}.

if.description: Conditional jump on a STORED ask answer: exactly one comparison (numeric gt/lt/gte/lte or string eq/ne) and a goto label. Fires only for live viewers — movies and skip-questions playback fall straight through. A backward jump must cross a quiz/ask so every loop has a human gate.

var.description: An earlier ask's store name (or t1.score).

goto.description: Label to jump to when the comparison holds.

test.description: With quiz, ask or flashcards: its test ("t1") — the card says "Question 2 of 5"; `results` scores the run.

flashcards.description: Self-check cards: {"flashcards": {"cards": [{"front": "вторник", "back": "Tuesday", "say": "вторник"}]}, "test": "t1"}. flip (default): flip, then Knew it / Unsure / Didn't. yesno: Know it / Don't, no back; ~1/3 fake: true invented words count against (vocabulary estimate). draw: how many at random; stop: the stop rule. Speak before and after, not per card.

results.description: A test's score card: {"results": {"test": "t1", "retry": true, "pass": 4}, "speak": "You got {t1.score} of {t1.total}."}. retry offers "Try the N missed" (each again, in place); pass adds Passed/Not yet. Publishes {t1.score}, {t1.total}, {t1.missed} (also for if). Movies: no card, all right.

lectures.description: With pass, in a test with a course: header: the lectures ("1-10") a pass marks known.

run.description: Play a controls script through a series of values while the speak lands — the movie form of a knob: {"run": {"code": "sim", "values": {"beta": {"from": 0.1, "to": 0.9, "steps": 5}, "gamma": 0.2}}, "speak": "Watch the peak move as the rate rises."}. values: per control name — a bare value holds, a list is the step values, {from, to, steps} walks from one to the other (snapped to the slider's step); the longest series sets the step count, shorter ones hold their last value; at most 20 steps. every: seconds per step (default: the speak's length divided by the steps, else 0.5). loop: repeat the series. The script and its drawn knobs STAY at the last values afterwards. Runs live in the app and in the movie; nothing is baked.

code.description: Id of a code element with controls.

values.description: Per control name: a value, a list, or {from, to, steps}.

loop.description: Play the series this many times.

smooth.description: Ranges glide by default: eased spacing and at least 10 steps (still ≤ 20). false plays the range in exactly `steps` linear jumps. Lists are never smoothed.

explore.description: Hold the lesson for the viewer: on a `pane: controls` script the drawn knobs are live and the tray stays shut; otherwise the beat opens exactly what it names (params: those sliders in the ⊕ tray; code: the editor card on that script's drawn pane); naming nothing on a figure played ON (piano, board, draggable parts) leaves the figure live, tray shut. The authored 'now try numbers yourself' moment, placed right after a personalized reveal. On a script with controls the beat first plays a short demo of the knobs (a seeded walk, or `play`'s planned sweep) with this speak over it; the app then stops with the knobs live, the movie continues. Without controls the beat is app-only and the movie skips it, speak included.

params.description: Slider param paths to show (default: all).

code.description: Id of a code element to open in the editor instead of the sliders: the viewer edits or replaces the script, presses Run, and sees the output pane and any template it feeds change; Continue restores the lesson. Place it right after the output beat.

game.description: Id of a code element that carries a `game`: the beat that hands the viewer the joystick — the emulator opens over the figure and the lesson waits until they close it. App only; movies skip the beat.

anatomy.description: On an anatomy figure: open the Body section of the explore tray — click a part to zoom into its region, breadcrumbs back, pills for layer, systems and names — and wait for Continue. The authored 'look around the body yourself' moment. App only; movies skip the beat.

activity.description: Start this named activity straight on the figure and wait until the viewer closes it: note_quiz, ear_key (piano), staff_find, staff_name, ear_staff (note_sheet), square_quiz, openings_drill, vs_computer, review_misses (chess: the puzzles this viewer missed, set again), element_quiz, group_quiz (periodic table), parts_quiz (any figure with named parts). The tray stays shut. App only; movies skip the beat.

goal.description: With activity vs_computer: play on from the board's position toward a goal — mate, promote (make a queen), win_material (amount points, default 1), hold (survive `within` moves without losing amount, default 2) — within N of the viewer's moves; the verdict is the score (1 of 1).

store.description: Keep what the viewer made under this name: an activity's score as {<store>} and {<store>.total}; on a note_sheet, the melody they composed as {<store>} — play it back with {"play": "{<store>}"}.

space.description: On a solar_system figure: open the Space section of the explore tray — click a planet or moon to look closer, breadcrumbs back out, pills for scale, names and date, a fact card with the Wikipedia summary. On a sky_map figure the same flag opens the sky's own section — click a star or a constellation to read about it, pills for the hour, the date and where you are standing. Either way the lesson waits for Continue. The authored 'look around yourself' moment. App only; movies skip the beat.

values.description: Per control name: a value, a list, or {from, to, steps}.

smooth.description: Ranges glide by default: eased spacing and at least 10 steps (still ≤ 20). false plays the range in exactly `steps` linear jumps. Lists are never smoothed.

play.description: The demo before the stop: omit for the seeded walk over the knobs, false for no demo, or {values, every, loop} (the run shape) for a planned sweep (unrelated to the music `play` verb).

label.description: A named position in the storyboard (snake_case), the target of quiz/ask right_goto/wrong_goto. Zero duration.

ask.description: Pose a question answered by TYPING. Check mode (answer set): the typed reply is judged, with optional retry and reveal. Collect mode (store set): the reply is saved and later speak lines may use {store_name} — e.g. 'Nice to meet you, {name}'. At least one of answer/store/on is required; default is REQUIRED with store, except with `on` (the movie types it). With `on` the viewer instead GUESSES A NUMBER ON THE FIGURE (see `on`). In video export the card types its answer by itself and never waits.

question.description: The question, spoken aloud and shown over the figure. When the page heading already asks it: only the task ("Click on the line.").

intro.description: Optional spoken introduction, prepended to the question line. Introduce an ask HERE, never in a separate speak command — viewers can skip questions, and a skipped question must take its introduction with it.

answer.description: Check mode: the correct answer, or a list of accepted ones (the first is revealed). Case, stress marks, ё/е and missing accents are ignored.

also.description: Machine-written from a list answer; on a say_it, other word orders accepted.

translit.description: A Cyrillic answer may also be typed in Latin letters (kot) — the default; false asks for Cyrillic.

accents.description: A missing accent (manana for mañana) is forgiven, the spelling shown; strict marks it wrong.

keyboard.description: false hides the Cyrillic keyboard a Cyrillic answer brings.

keys.description: The keyboard's active letters (those taught so far); must hold every letter of the answer.

right.description: One sentence stating the answer and the reason — spoken on a correct answer and as the reveal; no praise words.

wrong.description: Spoken on a wrong attempt. One sentence. Check mode only.

reveal.description: Check mode: speak the correct answer after a final wrong attempt (default true). A string/object: a stamp beside the figure WITH the reveal line (as quiz.reveal).

reveal_at.description: Where the reveal stamp goes: an element id (on it) or {x, y}.

above.description: Typed answer or multiple-choice listen: element id(s) shown with the question, in a band above the card (as quiz.above).

below.description: Typed answer or multiple-choice listen: element id(s) that land with the answer, under the card (as quiz.below).

frame.description: Typed answer or multiple-choice listen: as quiz.frame.

retry.description: Check mode: clear the field and ask again after a wrong attempt (default false). App only.

line.description: chess: a PUZZLE LINE — the rest of the board's `moves` from plies_shown (true) or that many plies. The viewer plays the side to move, the board replies; it ends at the line's end. No answer.

hints.description: chess: stepped hints, theme first, then the piece.

tries.description: chess line: misses per move before the board plays it (default 2).

accept.description: chess line: other first moves that also solve it (an ending with several wins).

themes.description: What it practises (fork, pin, back rank…), kept with the answer.

store.description: Save the typed reply under this snake_case name; use {name} in later speak lines.

default.description: Stand-in the movie types and skip/silent use. REQUIRED with store. A guess on a line: also where it starts.

required.description: App only: cannot be skipped without answering. Movies never wait.

widget.description: Answer device instead of typing: click = click the named element on the figure (answer = its id; the correct element GLOWS while right/the reveal is spoken, so you never need a highlight beat after a click question); piano = press a key on the drawn keyboard (answer = the note, e.g. C4); staff = click where a note goes on a note_sheet's staff (answer = the pitch, e.g. E4 — play it first for an ear question); chess = click two squares (answer = the move, e.g. e2e4); code = WRITE A SCRIPT on a code panel (implied by `code`, so you rarely write this one); drag = DRAG NAMES onto the figure (items = what to place, each judged where it lands; the answer is implied and `right` is required — it must say where each belongs; parts that were not drawn appear when the question ends, hits glow green and misses red); connect = DRAW A CONSTELLATION on a sky_map portrait (the viewer joins star to star — press one and drag to the next, or tap both — until the figure is made; answer = the constellation's element id, e.g. con_ori). Use it only with `focus` on that same figure, which is what gives every one of its stars an element id, and only AFTER AN EARLIER BEAT HAS DRAWN THE FIGURE — the lines are hidden while the question stands and drawn back as the reveal, so the task is "draw the one you just saw". The whole figure is required, exactly: every line and no extra one, since a wrong segment can be clicked away before Done. At most 24 lines — Orion's own count, and the most anyone will draw by hand; for a bigger figure ask which constellation it is instead. All but drag require answer. In movies the laser pointer demonstrates. Or the name of this drawcast's template (spec.template) when that template carries a widget body: the viewer works the figure and the widget's own answer is judged — in movies the widget's demo performs it.

items.description: With widget drag: what the viewer drags onto the figure — each an element id (an organ, a country_<slug>, any drawn part), a note on a piano figure (C4) or a square on a chess figure (e4), with an optional label for the chip (default: the id, humanised). 1–8 items, every one with a true place; leave the target parts UNDRAWN before the question when the task is to place them (they appear when it ends), or drawn when the task is to name what is there (a map).

tolerance.description: With widget drag: how far outside a target's outline a drop may land and still count, as a fraction of the target's size (default 0.25; 0 = inside only). With `on` (a guess): how close counts as right, as a fraction of the axis range (default 0.1) — or of the TRUE value with `relative: true`.

on.description: GUESS ON THE FIGURE: the viewer sets a number by hand on the figure, presses Answer, and the figure animates from their guess to the truth with the gap marked. Name what is guessed: a bar_chart bar (bar_3 — they drag its height), a line_chart line (line_1 — they draw the rest of it after `from`), a pie_chart slice (slice_2 — they drag its edge), a population state (crowd_sick — they drag how many are in it), a scale element's id (they click where the value lies), a list of these, or "all" (every bar, line or slice of the chart — scored by average error). The truth is the figure's own number: never write `answer` or `widget`. The guessed part must NOT be drawn before the ask (draw the axes and the other bars first); it appears when the question ends. Use store (e.g. store: g) and name the guess in right/wrong: {g} the guess, {g.true} the truth, {g.off} how far off, {g.pct} percent off. right is spoken when the guess is within tolerance, wrong otherwise — say both kindly. In movies the laser demonstrates `default` (a number, or numbers joined by commas) when given.

from.description: With `on` a line: the x value from which the viewer draws the rest of the line (default: the middle x). Before it the true line is shown.

predict.description: With `on`, right BEFORE an animate: the viewer predicts where that animate takes the figure — the guess starts where the figure stands now, the truth is the figure after the animate, and the animate itself plays from their prediction to the truth. The part may already be drawn.

readout.description: Market guess: false hides the live shift number while the copy is dragged.

gap.description: Guess: false = no gap number at the reveal.

revise.description: With `on`: start from an earlier guess on the same part (that ask's store), made with reveal: false — guess, show new evidence, guess again; the reveal shows both guesses and the truth. {store.moved} is how far they moved.

budget.description: With on: "all" on a bar_chart: the viewer SPLITS this total — each bar moves on its own, an account bar beside the plot shows what is left (red when overspent), and Answer waits until it balances. Pair with judge: false for 'how would you split it?'. {store.<bar_k>} keeps each share, {store.biggest} the label given most.

account_label.description: With budget: the account bar's label (default "Left"), in the cast's language.

judge.description: With `on`: false = an opinion with no right answer — no score, `right` is spoken whatever the guess, and the reveal shows the figure's own values as the reference (what is actually done). With `choose`: false = an opinion (which would YOU take?) — no answer, nothing scored.

choose.description: CHOOSE ON THE FIGURE: the options are things ALREADY DRAWN — a node, an icon, a group, a template part — and the viewer taps the thing itself (hover rings; Tab/Enter on the keyboard). Better than cards or a quiz whose choices repeat what the figure shows. answer = the right option's id (judged); judge: false = an opinion (store it: {c} is the tapped thing's label, {c.id} its id); {id, goto} options branch like decide cards and meet again at `then`. In movies the laser taps `default`, else the answer, else the first option.

then.description: With `choose` options that goto: the label after the branches where they meet again.

rule.description: With choose and answer (ODD ONE OUT over drawn things): what the others share — written under them as the odd one is ringed.

reveal_draw.description: Set by the odd-one-out expansion — never write it.

gaps.description: GAPS: the text or glossed text (or a list) whose [bracketed] pieces the viewer fills in, in order — typed on keys made from the answers, or tapped from chips (choices, or [ом]{ом,ой,ая} per gap). The blanks show until it is answered; then the right forms stand.

choices.description: gaps: chips to tap for every gap instead of typing.

count_each.description: gaps in a test: each gap counts as one question (default: the ask is one, right when every gap is).

gap_list.description: Set by the gaps expansion — never write it.

spot.description: SPOT IT ON THE PICTURE: the place the viewer taps — a region of the `on` image, a template part (liver, country_norway) or any drawn id; judged on its outline, the place outlined at the reveal. No answer or widget.

reveal_style.description: Reveal of a guess, cards, tree or formula: beside (default; the answer stays, the truth is drawn beside it), morph (the answer glides into the truth) or reorder (default for rank cards: they slide into the true order, a faint yours row behind).

reveal_order.description: all (default), or each: the truth part by part, 0.6 s apart.

keep.description: Guess: true keeps yours past the next question and a later animate (it follows the part).

after.description: The check's own slider, number line or cards after the answer: clear (leave) or keep. Default: a slider leaves; a scale or cards leave when the page goes on explaining.

stage.description: own: the rest of the figure fades while the question stands (cards or options over the figure).

confidence.description: With choose and answer: a bet, as on quiz.

poll.description: POLL: an opinion vs a study's answers — choices with shares (0–1), or on a scale with others; source: a sources id.

blanks.description: Tree: the parts of a decision_tree the viewer fills in — value_<node>, branchlabel_<parent>_<child>, effect_<node>, cost_<node>.

pick.description: Tree: the decision node whose best branch the viewer taps.

work.description: Tree: working lines under wrong blanks (default), "all" for every blank, or false for none.

check.description: Market guess (with `on` a supply or demand curve): what right means — direction, shape (default) or size.

others.description: Formula (on a math element with \blank): wrong tiles; the right contents are always tiles.

tile_size.description: Formula tiles' size (default: grows with the formula).

estimate.description: ESTIMATE SLIDER: a big counter over a slider (the ask draws it), scored like a guess on a scale. Never with on.

form.description: Formula, typed: "exact" compares the written form, not the value.

feedback.description: This question's own feedback (as the top-level feedback; wins over it).

say_question.description: false: the question is neither spoken nor shown.

release.description: With `on`: letting go of the drag is the answer (default true). false shows an Answer button, so the viewer can adjust before answering — for a careful estimate. Several parts (on: all, a whole pie) always get the button.

relative.description: With `on`: tolerance is a fraction of the true value (within 20 % = tolerance 0.2) — for money and other quantities spanning orders of magnitude.

code.description: Ask the viewer to WRITE CODE: the id of a code element they type into — normally an empty or stubbed panel (`code: ""` or one comment line, `show: "left"`, `frame: "screen"`) drawn on an earlier beat. The panel's own editor opens on it, the viewer runs their script and presses Check, and what `expect` reads is compared with `answer`.
