Everything else about an ask still applies: right/wrong lines, retry, required, store, right_goto/wrong_goto. Movies and embeds skip the question, so the `right` line must state the answer for a viewer who never types.

expect.description: With `code`: what the viewer's run has to say — "stdout" (what it printed; THE DEFAULT — pair it with a question that says what to print), "figure" (answer "1" when the script must draw a plot), or a VARIABLE the script leaves behind ("total", "df.mean" for a DataFrame column's mean — the same paths the {id.var} data bridge harvests). Numbers compare as numbers, so 45, 45.0 and 4.5e1 are one answer — but ask for a value the script can hit exactly (an integer, or a rounded number the question names).

right_goto.description: Jump to this label on a correct VIEWER answer. Movies always play straight through.

wrong_goto.description: Jump to this label on a wrong VIEWER answer — typically back to the explanation, so the viewer re-watches and the question comes again. Movies always play straight through.

listen.description: LISTEN: a line the viewer hears but does not see, which the question is about — answered by options + correct, on + correct, or answers. reveal: true stamps its words at the answer. A list of lines: one clip in their voices. "same": another question on the clip before.

transcript.description: listen: no words after the last question.

options.description: listen: the choices, a few words each.

shuffle.description: listen options: as a quiz's shuffle (false: as written).

correct.description: listen: 1-based — the right one of options, or of the drawn ids in on.

answers.description: listen: dictation — the viewer types what they heard; the accepted spellings.

say_it.description: SAY IT: the line the viewer says aloud, records and compares with the native clip, then rates; question optional. reveal: true stamps the line after the take.

show.description: say_it: the card shows the line (text, default), the gloss as a cue (cue), or nothing (none).

voice.description: listen / say_it: whose voice says the line (default a).

gloss.description: listen: the line's translation, shown after the answer; say_it: the cue.

lang.description: listen / say_it: BCP-47 tag of the line, for the speech recogniser only.

show.description: Element ids to make visible instantly (inverse of hide; no animation).

hide.description: Element ids to make invisible instantly. Hidden elements still exist and can be shown again.

erase.description: Element ids to remove with a reverse hand-drawn (un-sketch) animation, then keep hidden.

clear.description: Hide everything currently visible. Use {} to clear all, or keep to leave some ids on screen.

keep.description: Ids to leave visible (e.g. the axes).

pane.description: Book only: figure (default), notes (the text pane) or both.

write.description: Book only: a block of Markdown written into the text pane as the paired speak starts. A string, or {id, text, temp}: id names it for highlight/erase/point; temp = a scratch note, gone before the next block.

view.description: Book only: give the book to one pane, or share it again.

card.description: The opening heading: centred at the top of the page, underlined, zooming quickly from large to its size, and it stays (a later heading card replaces it; no need to erase the old one) — then get straight to the first drawing. Keep its speak to a few words, or none. style "center" is the slower TV-style card for a long lecture: sketched mid-canvas with a subtitle, a push-in, then un-drawn.

subtitle.description: A quieter line under it (style center only).

highlight.description: Temporarily emphasize visible elements, then return to normal. With a paired speak and no duration it LIGHTS UP AND HOLDS for the rest of the sentence, releasing as the voice ends — the way to talk about one specific element (a curve, an equilibrium) while it is lit.

effect.description: glow (default) = suits the target: a yellow band under a line, a marker behind a code line, red ink on a formula, text or shape; circle = a hand-drawn ring; underline = a pen line under it; strike = a pen line through it (while the voice speaks; a lasting cross-out is an annotation); pulse = red ink that throbs three times first. box = a box drawn round the target; soft_light = on a picture place, the place lifted with a soft light, the rest untouched (the default there); outline = a thin oval round a picture place; light = a stronger wash of light over the place (with rest dim, grey, blur or paper it also changes the rest of the picture) — once or twice per cast at most; ring = a hand-drawn ring, detail = the place enlarged beside the picture (in the paper a tall painting leaves; over a far corner of a wide one), tied to it by two lines; magnify = a picture place enlarged where it stands for its sentence, then let back — for a small detail the voice describes. color replaces the red/yellow.

part.description: Only this piece: a formula term as TeX ("t_r"), or text of a label or code line — any case, every occurrence; ^/$ anchor to a word's start/end, [ ] marks one piece of the key.

duration.description: Seconds. Omit with a paired speak to let the effect last the whole sentence (default 1.5 otherwise).

lift.description: Start this mark fresh instead of gliding from the previous one on the same picture.

keep.description: Book text: the mark stays (else it goes at the next block). strike = a line through a text block.

strength.description: Picture places: how hard the light presses — soft, normal, strong, spotlight, or 0..1.

rest.description: Picture places: the rest of the picture stays as it is (none, the default: only the place brightens), dims, goes grey, blurs, or sinks into the paper.

focus.description: The inverse spotlight: dim every OTHER visible element while the targets stay at full strength — the way a hand on a whiteboard says 'ignore the rest'. With a paired speak and no duration, the focus HOLDS FOR THE WHOLE SENTENCE. Use it to walk a dense figure region by region.

target.description: Element ids that stay lit; everything else dims.

duration.description: Seconds. Omit with a paired speak to hold for the sentence (default 2 otherwise).

lift.description: Start this mark fresh instead of gliding from the previous one on the same picture.

strength.description: How far the rest recedes: soft, normal, strong, spotlight, or 0..1.

rest.description: Picture places: the rest stays as it is (none, the default: only the place brightens), dims, goes grey, blurs, or sinks into the paper.

point.description: A laser pointer travels to the target and gestures at it, then disappears. Combine with speak blocking:false to talk while pointing.

at.description: Where: {"ref": id, "anchor": name}, {"x": …, "y": …}, {"data": [x, y]} for a spot on a chart, or {"canvas": [x, y]} — an object, not [x, y].

gesture.description: tap = dip at the spot (default); circle = trace a ring around it; underline = sweep beneath it. On a picture place: arrow = a hand-drawn arrow (its default), glow = a soft glow.

lift.description: Start this mark fresh instead of gliding from the previous one on the same picture.

move.description: Translate and/or rotate and/or scale elements: by a delta, to a destination, along a path, by rotate degrees, or scale by a factor. Attached labels FOLLOW a translation (they do not rotate); intersection points, regions and other derived elements do not — redraw those.

by.description: [dx, dy] delta — domain units when a domain is declared, else logical units.

path.description: Waypoint offsets from the element's starting position (same units as by); the last waypoint is the final offset. Use instead of by for curved or multi-leg motion.

to.description: Destination of the moving element's `anchor` (default its centre) — instead of by/path — e.g. "to": {"ref": "a", "anchor": "tip"} with "anchor": "tail" puts b's tail on a's tip — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

anchor.description: With to: which anchor of the MOVING element lands there (default center) — "anchor": "tail" to place an arrow's tail.

rotate.description: Turn the element by this many DEGREES, counter-clockwise, about `pivot` (default: its own centre) — e.g. {"move": {"target": ["slice_3"], "rotate": 180, "duration": 1}} flips a slice. Combine with by/to to slide and turn at once.

pivot.description: With rotate/scale: the point to turn or grow about — {"anchor": "vertex_2"} (no ref) is the element's OWN vertex; {"ref": "wheel"} another element's centre; rides along with by/to, so by + rotate rolls. Omit for the element's own centre — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

scale.description: Grow or shrink the element by this factor about `pivot` (default its own centre), cumulative across moves — e.g. "scale": 2 doubles it in place, 0.5 halves it. Combine with rotate/by/to.

trail.description: Leave the TRACK of the motion as a new element <id>_trail (the locus): true traces the first target's centre; {"of": "dot", "anchor": "bottom"} traces that target's anchor — a point on a rolling wheel draws the cycloid, a planet its orbit. Fade, erase or highlight the trail afterwards by its id.

ghost.description: Ghost of the targets before they move — KEEP a faded copy of the original where it is while this plays: true keeps every target at 0.3, ["id", …] keeps those, {"of": […], "opacity": 0.2} sets the shade. The copy is an element <id>_ghost you can erase or fade later — a pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default: nothing is kept.

arrange.description: Lay the targets out and animate them there — code computes every position and turn. layout: row (left to right), zipper (sector pieces alternately up and down, interleaved into the πr² rectangle), fan (sectors side by side about ONE apex — the angle-sum proof), grid, ring, hex (a honeycomb), stack. target may be ONE pieces id for all its pieces. at = the centre of the arrangement (default: where the targets are now; fan: the first sector's apex). {"arrange": {"target": "kake", "layout": "zipper", "at": [650, 375], "duration": 3}, "speak": "Now we zip the slices together…"}

target.description: Element ids, or one pieces id.

layout.description: Pick the shape the targets end up in — e.g. "layout": "zipper" interleaves sector pieces into a rectangle, "fan" sets torn-off corner angles side by side about one point, "hex" packs hexagons into a honeycomb, "row" lines them up left to right, "unroll" straightens ring pieces into strips stacked bottom-up (innermost first) — the circumference-equals-length proof.

at.description: Centre of the arrangement (default: where the targets are now; fan: the first sector's apex) — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

start.description: fan: the angle where the first piece begins, degrees counter-clockwise from +x — e.g. "start": 0 lays the angles along a horizontal line rightwards (default 0).

gap.description: Space between neighbours in logical units (default 6; hex defaults to 0 for a tight comb) — e.g. "gap": 20 for an airy row. fan's sectors always touch; gap applies only to non-sector targets there.

columns.description: grid: pieces per row — e.g. "columns": 4 lays twelve pieces out four wide.

ghost.description: Ghost of the targets before they move — KEEP a faded copy of the original where it is while this plays: true keeps every target at 0.3, ["id", …] keeps those, {"of": […], "opacity": 0.2} sets the shade. The copy is an element <id>_ghost you can erase or fade later — a pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default: nothing is kept.

fade.description: Persistently dim elements (or restore them with to: 1) so the rest stands out — e.g. {"fade": {"target": ["supply"], "to": 0.25, "duration": 1}, "speak": "Set supply aside for a moment."}. Attached labels fade with their element. It stays until the next fade; use hide to remove an element, focus/highlight for a momentary emphasis that ends by itself.

target.description: Element ids, or one pieces id.

to.description: Opacity to settle at — e.g. 0.25 dims, 1 restores.

flip.description: Reflect elements across a mirror line, played as a turn-over — the fourth transformation beside slide, turn and grow: {"flip": {"target": ["tri"], "axis": "vertical"}} mirrors about a vertical line through the element's own centre; "line": {"from": {"ref": "axis", "anchor": "start"}, "to": {"ref": "axis", "anchor": "end"}} mirrors across a drawn line. Attached labels follow (they never turn over themselves).

target.description: Element ids, or one pieces id.

axis.description: The mirror line's direction through `through` (default vertical).

through.description: A point the mirror line passes through (default: the target's own centre; {"anchor": "left"} with no ref is the target's own left edge) — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

line.description: An explicit mirror line from one point to another — overrides axis/through.

from.description: One point on the line — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

to.description: Another point on the line — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

ghost.description: Ghost of the targets before they move — KEEP a faded copy of the original where it is while this plays: true keeps every target at 0.3, ["id", …] keeps those, {"of": […], "opacity": 0.2} sets the shade. The copy is an element <id>_ghost you can erase or fade later — a pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default: nothing is kept.

morph.description: Change an element's SHAPE smoothly: {"morph": {"target": ["para"], "to": {"ref": "rekt"}}} slides a parallelogram's outline into the rectangle (shearing — the stack of cards); "stretch": [2, 1] with "pivot": {"anchor": "left"} doubles the width from the left edge (non-uniform scaling — move.scale is uniform); "to": [[x, y], …] gives the outline; "reset": true goes back; "tex": "new TeX" retypesets a math element, tweening glyph-by-glyph. Works on polygon, path, sector, arc, curve, region and pieces; a shape circle/rect cannot morph — declare a polygon.

target.description: Element ids, or one pieces id.

to.description: The new outline — [[x, y], …] in canvas coordinates (domain units when a domain is declared), or {"ref": id} for another element's outline as it is now.

stretch.description: [sx, sy] factors about pivot — e.g. [2, 1] doubles the width only.

pivot.description: With stretch: the fixed point (default the element's centre; {"anchor": "bottom_left"} without ref is its own corner) — [x, y] (domain units when a domain is declared, else canvas), {"data": [x, y]}, {"canvas": [x, y]} (canvas units always), or {"ref": id, "anchor": name} for a point ON an element so you never compute it: center (default) / top / bottom / left / right / top_left / top_right / bottom_left / bottom_right on any element; polygon vertex_1…, side_1… (side midpoints), centroid; sector apex, arc, start, end; arrow and edge tail, tip, mid; path start, end, mid, point_1…; angle vertex, arc; ellipse focus_1, focus_2; line start, end, mid, point_1….

reset.description: Back to the layout's own points.

tex.description: New TeX for a math element — retypesets, tweening glyph-by-glyph from the current TeX.

ghost.description: Ghost of the targets before they move — KEEP a faded copy of the original where it is while this plays: true keeps every target at 0.3, ["id", …] keeps those, {"of": […], "opacity": 0.2} sets the shade. The copy is an element <id>_ghost you can erase or fade later — a pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default: nothing is kept.

step.description: Write the next line of a math element's `steps`: {"step": "eq", "speak": "…"} — the last line is copied one line down and morphs into the next TeX while the sentence plays. {"step": {"target": "eq", "in_place": true}} rewrites the current line instead (a substitution).

copy.description: Clone an element under a new id, visible where the source now stands: {"copy": {"target": "eq", "as": "eq2"}} — the clone can then be moved, arranged or morphed independently of the original.

as.description: The clone's new id (default target_copy, then _copy_2, …).

flow.description: Something STREAMS along strokes while the sentence lands — money round the circular flow, current in a circuit, blood, water, traffic, infection along a contact: {"flow": {"along": ["wages", "spending"]}, "speak": "Money circulates…"}. Transient like highlight; with a paired speak and no duration it runs until the voice ends. "reverse": true streams the other way; "kind": "dashes" for a pulse rather than particles.

along.description: Stroke element ids to stream along (arrows, edges, paths, curves, arcs).

duration.description: Seconds (default 3; omit with a paired speak to hold until the voice ends).

speed.description: Logical units per second (default 120) — 40 reads as a trickle, 300 as a rush.

kind.description: dots = particles (default); dashes = a moving pulse.

reverse.description: Stream from the stroke's end to its start.

keep.description: Keep a faded copy of elements where they are NOW, as elements <id>_ghost — the original stays on screen while its pieces move away: {"keep": {"target": "kake"}, "speak": "Keep the circle in mind while the slices move."} before an arrange or a morph. A pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default opacity 0.3.

target.description: Element ids, or one pieces id.

opacity.description: Shade of the kept copy (default 0.3) — e.g. 0.5 for a stronger ghost.

camera.description: Zoom/pan the view. Set reset:true to return to the full canvas (on a template wider than the page: its whole world).

center.description: Arrow/edge endpoint: set ref to an element id or a picture place ("art:railing", "art@[0.3, 0.6]" — never page x/y read off a frame), OR x+y (domain units if a domain is declared, else canvas), OR data: [x, y] (data units — also a template's axes), OR canvas: [x, y] (canvas units, even on a domain page).

on.description: Frame these elements (one id or several, e.g. a subtree): zoom "fit" on their union unless zoom is a number.

zoom.description: Magnification: 1 = one page, 2 = 2× (default 2 when centering); "fit" frames center.ref (or on) with a margin.

animate.description: Smoothly animate NUMERIC template params to these target values while the paired speak lands. Keys are dot paths into params (e.g. {"demand_shift.amount": 25} or {"azimuth": 240}); the whole figure re-computes every frame, so intersections, guides, and regions move honestly. Always write the STARTING value explicitly in params (e.g. demand_shift: {amount: 0}). Only for template specs. A data template's stage param is the canonical target ({"stage": 1}); array entries address as values.2. "box" may instead be a region name — {"animate": {"box": "right"}} shrinks the figure into that half over the beat; write the starting "box" (e.g. "full") in params.

duration.description: With animate: seconds the animation takes (default 2).

easing.description: With animate: velocity profile over the whole tween (default: today's smoothstep). A long race (many seconds) reads better as "linear" — constant speed — than the default's ease in/out, which blurs the middle and crawls at the ends.

ghost.description: With animate: ghost of the figure at this boundary — KEEP a faded copy of the original where it is while this plays: true keeps every target at 0.3, ["id", …] keeps those, {"of": […], "opacity": 0.2} sets the shade. The copy is an element <id>_ghost you can erase or fade later — a pieces id ghosts every piece: kake_1_ghost, kake_2_ghost, … Default: nothing is kept.

of.description: The element whose point is traced.

trail.description: With animate: leave the track of that point across the sweep as the element <of>_trail; erase or fade it by id later.

play.description: Play synthesized notes while the paired speak lands (or on their own). Either ONE notation string — space-separated notes "C4:q E4:q G4:h" (pitch letter + optional #/b + octave 1-7, duration w/h/q/e/s = 4/2/1/½/¼ beats, chords joined with + as in C4+E4+G4:h, R for a rest) — up to four parallel voices [{"notes": "...", "instrument": "piano"}] that start together (melody over bass) — or a whole tune as {"abc": "K:C\nC D E F|…"} in ABC notation. ONLY for figures genuinely about sound or music.

abc.description: A whole tune in ABC notation (K:/M:/L:/Q: headers, then the music; V: voices become parallel channels). Tempo comes from Q: unless the command sets tempo.

instrument.description: With play: the synthesized instrument (default tone; array voices can override per voice).

reveal.description: With play: element ids revealed IN TIME with the notes and KEPT — id k appears exactly when the k-th sounding note of the first voice starts and stays visible (staff notes accumulating as the tune plays).

press.description: With play: element ids PRESSED in time with the notes — id k appears when the k-th sounding note starts and DISAPPEARS when it ends, like a piano key going down and back up. Combine with reveal (e.g. reveal staff notes, press piano keys).

commands.description: The playback sequence: narration (speak), drawing (draw/pause), and gesture verbs (highlight/point/move/show/hide/erase/clear/camera/card/animate). Elements not mentioned in any draw/show/hide/erase command are drawn at the end automatically.
